item: W10 instruction imports: link vetting before an import is read
coordinateUnit: zero-based UTF-16, left-closed/end-exclusive, over the decoded module text
readAs: inert data; no recovered entrypoint was executed

facts.name: vetting walk
facts.note: for(let o=0;o<Un;o+=1); visited Set; a repeated state returns false

facts.name: not-UTF-8 refusal
facts.text: link body is not valid UTF-8

facts.name: climbs-out refusal
facts.text: link body climbs out of a directory it entered

facts.name: too-long refusal
facts.text: link chain too long to vet

facts.name: separator set
facts.note: j===ge.sep?/[\\/]+/:\/\/+ - both separators only on the backslash platform

portedInvariant: An instruction file that is reached through a link is vetted before it is read as instructions: a body that is not valid UTF-8 is refused, a body that enters a directory and climbs back out is refused, a repeated state is refused as a cycle, and a chain past 32 hops is refused by name.

wiring.note: first statement of the nested-import reader, the root-file reader and loadPathInstructions' visit, so a refused link is refused for every reader that would have taken the file

ownedDecisions: The bound is kept at 32 hops, the recovered local, rather than reusing the file-tool resolver's 64.
The not-UTF-8 rule is a fatal decode of the raw link bytes rather than a replacement-character test on the decoded text.
A repeated state is refused by name as a cycle; the recovered walk returns false so its cloud-session caller can count a chain it will not send.
Both separators count on every platform, so docs\..\other.md is refused on a POSIX host; the recovered set makes that platform-dependent.
The refusal is a LinkVetError carrying its reason, wrapped by config.ts into a ConfigError naming the file, so it arrives on the tool call that triggered instruction loading.
notPorted: The true/false result of On and the counters its caller fills from it (symlink_not_sent, too_many_links): verdicts about what a cloud session may receive.
The home_unvettable and outside_root states of the same module, which belong to the same handoff.

asserts: control: the import reached through a link inside its own directory reaches the second request
refused: the same import through a link that enters docs and climbs back out fails the read with 'climbs out of a directory it entered'
the refused import never reaches a request

identity.independentOfflineRebuild: fresh directory, source bundle of 208 files, npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline, check and build, identical merged digest

regressions: None. The first version of the integration case built the climbing link body with path.join, which normalizes the `..` segments away and produced a link that did not climb; the body is now written verbatim.
limitations: Vetting covers links on the instruction-import path only; a link on the path of a file a tool reads is resolved by the W09 resolver, whose rules are its own.
No real network mount, Windows host or chain past either bound was observed.
